facts.text: On this date in 1842, China signed the Treaty of Nanking, ceding Hong Kong to Britain — a handover that lasted exactly 155 years until 1997.
On Aug 29, 2005, Hurricane Katrina made landfall. New Orleans sits up to 6 meters below sea level, making it one of the most geologically vulnerable cities on Earth.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Dhaka, Bangladesh than inside one the same size drawn around Tokyo — density, not raw size, is what makes a megacity.
Canada has more lakes than every other country on Earth combined, holding roughly 60% of the world's fresh surface water within its borders.
The city of Surat, India processes over 90% of the world's rough diamonds — yet almost no one outside the trade knows its name.

On this day in 1966, the Beatles played their final paid concert at Candlestick Park — the same year their Apple Corps royalty disputes with EMI began a legal saga that dragged on for four decades and hundreds of millions in claims.

On August 29, 2005, Hurricane Katrina made landfall. Insurance payouts eventually exceeded $41 billion, making it the costliest natural disaster claim event in U.S. history at the time — and permanently repricing Gulf Coast risk.

The New York Stock Exchange was founded under a buttonwood tree in 1792 with just 24 brokers. Today it lists companies whose combined market cap exceeds the GDP of every nation on Earth except the U.S. itself.

Berkshire Hathaway was originally a failing textile company. Warren Buffett later called buying it the worst investment of his career — a mistake he estimates cost him over $200 billion in compounded opportunity.

The entire global bond market, roughly $130 trillion, is larger than the stock market yet almost invisible to ordinary investors — most of the world's borrowing happens in a market they will never directly see or touch.
On this date in 1831, Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction — the phenomenon that still generates virtually all electricity on Earth today.
On August 29, 2005, Katrina made landfall. The storm's pressure drop caused the Gulf floor to flex measurably under gravitational load.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh about a billion tons.
Your body replaces the lining of your small intestine every two to four days — one of the fastest cell turnover rates of any tissue you have.
Light from the Sun takes eight minutes to reach you, but the photons themselves were generated by fusion reactions that began their journey to the surface 100,000 years ago.
On this day in 1831, Faraday demonstrated electromagnetic induction — the principle powering every generator on Earth — using equipment simpler than a middle school science kit.
Fax machines were in commercial use by 1865, twelve years before the telephone existed.
On this day in 2005, Hurricane Katrina made landfall. The levees that failed had been flagged as catastrophically inadequate in a FEMA report published the year before.
The woolly mammoth was still alive on a Russian island when the Egyptians were building the pyramids. The overlap lasted 1,000 years.
Charlie Chaplin's 'The Kid,' released in 1921, is older than sliced bread, which wasn't sold until 1928.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012. Already it feels ancient.
Hiraeth (Welsh): a homesickness for a home you cannot return to, or never had. Untranslatable because English has never needed to sit with that particular ache long enough to name it.

On this day in 1831, Faraday demonstrated electromagnetic induction — and the word 'electricity' itself descends from the Greek 'elektron,' meaning amber, the substance ancients rubbed to produce sparks.
Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word from Tierra del Fuego meaning a look shared by two people who both want something but neither will initiate. The Yaghan language now has one fluent native speaker.
Vellichor (n.): the strange wistfulness of used bookshops. Another Koenig coinage — proof that naming a feeling is sometimes the only way to prove it was real.
On Aug 29, 2017, Bitcoin Cash completed its first difficulty adjustment after the fork — dropping 43% in one epoch, a stress test no model had anticipated at that scale.
On Aug 29, 2021, Ethereum's EIP-1559 had been live for 24 days and had already burned over 100,000 ETH, retiring the fixed-fee auction model that had defined the network for six years.

The Bitcoin genesis block's coinbase contains the text 'The Times 03/Jan/2009 Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — embedded not as metadata but as raw script data, unspendable and permanent.
Ethereum's state trie is not stored on-chain. Full nodes reconstruct it locally from transaction history; the trie itself has never existed in a block, only its root hash has.
The 2010 'value overflow' bug let one transaction mint 184 billion BTC from thin air. Satoshi patched it within hours via a hard fork — the only time Bitcoin consensus was rolled back in its history.

On this date in 2012, Alex Krizhevsky submitted AlexNet to the ImageNet competition. It cut the error rate nearly in half, from 26% to 15.3% — a gap so large the field assumed a bug before accepting it was real.

On this date in 2016, DeepMind published its WaveNet paper, generating raw audio waveforms sample-by-sample at 16,000 Hz — too slow for real-time by a factor of 1,000, yet still deployed in Google Assistant two years later.
GPT-4 training is estimated to have consumed around 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity — roughly the annual consumption of 4,500 American homes — before a single user query was served.
The original transformer paper, 'Attention Is All You Need,' was rejected from ICLR 2017 before being accepted at NeurIPS. It has since accumulated over 150,000 citations.

AlphaFold 2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins — essentially the entire known protein universe — in under a year. Experimental methods had produced roughly 170,000 structures across the prior six decades.
